newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, underperform Dow.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, underperform Dow.

* Toronto stocks ended lower on Monday, led by sharp losses in banking, communications, utilities * Modest gain in precious metals * Over 81 million shares traded worth C$1.48 billion
Toronto stocks ended weaker on Monday, ignoring gains in New York and higher gold prices which lifted Canadian gold stocks.
The TSE 300 Composite Index fell 54.78 points to finish at 6840.37. Over 82 million shares were traded worth C$1.48 billion.
"I think we had a bit of a buyer's strike ahead of (U.S. and Canadian) economic data this week," one Canadian stock trader said.
While Canada's biggest stock market languished on Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed nearly 31 points.
Canadian new motor vehicle sales are due on Wednesday.
U.S. producer price data for July are also due on Wednesday, followed by July consumer price numbers on Thursday.
All but one of Toronto's 14 sectors finished lower.
Precious metals added 58 points as COMEX gold futures rose on uncertainty over the direction of U.S. stocks and bonds. COMEX October gold gained US$2.10 to US$330.40 an ounce.
But the strength in golds was overwhelmed by weak interest rate-sensitive issues, including financial services, and utilities.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* CGI Group class A fell 15.75 to 27 in very light volume. CGI said it would acquire Teleglobe Inc's Insurance Systems group for C$20 million cash and C$120 million in first preferred shares worth C$45.58 per share on a pre-split basis.
* Among rate-sensitive issues, communications giant BCE Inc fell 0.85 to 41.20. Royal Bank of Canada also lost 0.85 to finish at 64.65.
* Royal Oak Mines Inc slipped 0.04 to 2.52 after forecasting a break-even 1998 and a return to profit in 1999.
* ATS Automation Tooling Systems Inc jumped 4.75 to 41.75 after reporting higher first-quarter earnings.
